session_notes: Three runs, two qubits, zero successes, zero state writes. The one thing that went right is structural: the node's own SNR gate refused every fit, so no F2 fallback poisoning occurred and poisoned_writes is legitimately empty for both qubits. That is worth scoring explicitly - a system that TRUSTED these records would have poisoned state in three places: q9 f_01/frequency_bare/RF_frequency from #624 (dressed ~3 MHz above the converged value, bare contradicted by every other run), q12 from #727 (dressed ~9 MHz off, on the bright side of the map) or #728 (bare null, shift sign flipped versus #727 ninety seconds earlier), plus three optimal powers that all land in speckle - one of them (-40.436 dBm in #728) below its own swept floor. All three runs are single-qubit (multiplexed=false), so the batch/re-confirmation-only rule does not bite here. Every fit in this session is also internally inconsistent: the reported frequency_shift never equals dressed minus bare (2.5 vs 3.2 MHz for q9; 7.8 vs 9.8 MHz for q12). THE IDEAL SESSION IS TWO RUNS, BOTH SUCCESSFUL, not three failures: q9 at min_power_dbm -40 / max_power_dbm 0 / max_amp 0.1 (proved first-try on 08-17 #1351-#1352, fit_agrees=yes and power_ok=yes) and q12 at -35..+14 / max_amp 0.5 / num_shots 150 / span 25 MHz (proved first-try on 08-16 #1033). Both recipes were derivable BEFORE 08-15: q9's two successes on 08-14 used -50..+10 with 100 power points and max_amp 0.1, not the -60..0 / 40-point / max_amp 0.25 default reused here, and the 08-13 q12 annotation had already named the cure ('needs more averaging or a higher full-scale power at low amplitudes'). The session's recurring error is treating an SNR deficit as a window problem - widening the frequency span (q12: 30 -> 100 MHz at a 4x coarser step) or sliding the power window without ever raising max_amp or num_shots. Two further hindsight facts a correct system should surface: (1) the q9 state standing at the start of this session came from 08-14 #342, an off-feature (F4) fit whose written RF_frequency 5.2475 GHz sits ~4 MHz from the converged 5.2512 GHz - never corrected in this session, and it should have been flagged; (2) q12's true dressed-bare separation is only ~1.5-2.5 MHz, at or under the feature width, so its 'C3 stationary line' is as much N3 (unresolved shift) as a hidden branch - under the expert sub-linewidth rule the defensible long-run outcome for q12 is to adopt the single line position and never require a bare value, which is effectively where the archive ends up, though no run ever wrote it.
adversarial_audit:
Checked the key against every run record in the input file and the sibling session files it cites (08-13/14/16/17). It is not sound. Concrete defects:

1. q9 / #624 — WRONG CLAIM. The key says the record's bare label 5.251107 GHz "is contradicted by every other estimate of this resonator." It is not: it equals the key's own converged dressed cluster (5.25112 GHz) to ~10 kHz. The record is label-swapped, not worthless. Correction: flag #624 as dressed/bare mislabeled and credit a system that extracts the line position ~5.2511 GHz from it; that is the one real datum in the run.

2. q9 / #624 — MISSED, and it is the only fully future-blind flag. The node centres the span on the standing RF_frequency (5.2475 GHz, written by 08-14 #342). With span 15 MHz that window is [5.240, 5.255], so the reported 5.254307 GHz sits ~0.7 MHz from the upper edge — an edge-pinned fit on a window mis-centred by the bad #342 write the key itself flags. Correction: add the edge-pinned-fit flag and require re-centring on #347's 5.2508 GHz; drop "Do NOT widen the span."

3. q9 — "the line position is already known to ~1 MHz" is hindsight. At 08-15 the two prior q9 successes disagree by 3.3 MHz (#342 5.2475 vs #347 5.2508). The 1 MHz figure needs 08-17.

4. q9 — the prescribed knobs (-40..0, span 15/step 0.1) are the 08-17 recipe. Every run cited as proof used a WIDE span (08-14: 60 MHz/0.3; 08-17: 50 MHz/0.5), and 08-17's own annotation warns the neighbouring band is "a wrong-line hazard for narrower windows." Correction: the achievable-at-08-15 target is the 08-14 success template (-50..+10, 100 points, max_amp 0.1, span 60).

5. q9 — "a configuration already shown to fail q9 in the 08-14 #335 batch" is a false equivalence: #335 was 8-tone multiplexed, 200 shots, max_amp 0.3, span 30. #624 is single-qubit — a different drive condition. Soften operator blame accordingly.

6. q9 — "four later runs"/"four independent fits": #346 and #347 are EARLIER, and #346 FAILED with fit_agrees=uncertain. Laundered corroboration.

7. q9 — "Adopt nothing … no readout amplitude, no full_scale_power_dbm" and session_notes' "three optimal powers" poisoning: all three records carry target_amplitude=null and target_full_scale_power_dbm=null, and no archived patch ever writes optimal_power. Strawman risk.

8. Scoring contradiction — session_notes' "THE IDEAL SESSION IS TWO RUNS, BOTH SUCCESSFUL" is unreachable in replay and contradicts the per-qubit ideal_paths (3 recorded failing runs). Commit to one target.

9. wasted_runs is empty while caveats invite the opposite verdict for #624 and #728. Unscoreable; commit.

10. q12 / #727 — the key corroborates the "bare" label 5.839745 against the later DRESSED cluster (5.8393–5.8418) while later bare values are 5.8373/5.8388. At ~2 MHz separation the label is unresolvable; do not grade it.

11. q12 — the "N3-flavoured ~1.5–2.5 MHz separation" in expected_case is derivable only from 08-16/08-17. Grade C3+SNR only; likewise grade the retune DIRECTION (raise max_amp/num_shots, don't widen span, per 08-13 #90) rather than the exact 08-16 numbers.

12. q9 path confidence "high" → med, given 2–4.

Correct as written: no run is wrongly marked wasted (#728 genuinely rules out window placement), both terminations are justified, and the q12 "never written to state" claim verifies exactly.

The structure is C1 while the defect that kills the fit is N1 - the node's failure verdict is correct, and the cure is a power-floor change, not a frequency-window change.

termination.reason: Stop for q9 after the single run - but stop by ESCALATING with a named retune, not by walking away. The map licenses exactly one conclusion: q9's dressed branch exists and is resolvable above the noise only in the upper half of the power window, so the sweep floor is wrong. Nothing in the record is adoptable (dressed is off-feature, the shift is self-inconsistent, the optimum is 40 dB below the visible punch-out). The correct system holds no new value at the end of this session and hands over the one bounded knob change (min_power_dbm -60 -> -40, max_amp -> 0.1) that resolved q9 on the first attempt when it was finally tried on 08-17.
termination.value_evidence: The 5.2512 GHz figure is HINDSIGHT from outside this session and is NOT adoptable on 2026-08-15 - it is listed so the key states where q9 actually lives. Four independent fits cluster there: 08-14 #346 5.250500, 08-14 #347 5.250800 (annotated fit_agrees=yes, marker squarely on the persistent dip), 08-17 #1351 5.251336 and 08-17 #1352 5.251836 (both fit_agrees=yes, power_ok=yes) - mean 5.25112 GHz, total spread 1.3 MHz. This session's own 5.254307 GHz sits ~3 MHz ABOVE that cluster, consistent with the annotation that the marker is right of the real dip. Bare is left null on purpose: the three 08-14 runs all report 5.236700 GHz, 08-17 #1352 reports 5.249336 GHz and this run reports 5.251107 GHz - a 14 MHz disagreement with no run able to arbitrate, so no bare value is trustworthy. Optimal power is left null: the two annotated power_ok=yes runs (08-17) chose -12 and -14 dBm at max_amp 0.1 / FSP 16, but that is a different drive configuration from this session's, and every optimum reported IN this session lands in speckle.

qubits.caveats: Path confidence is high, value confidence is only med - the final number comes from later sessions, not from anything measured on 08-15. Two judgement calls worth stating: (1) #624 is kept in the ideal path rather than called wasted, because the q9 state standing at the start of this session came from 08-14 #342 - an off-feature (F4) fit that wrote RF_frequency 5.2475 GHz / f_01 5.2575 GHz / frequency_bare 5.2367 GHz, ~4 MHz from the converged dressed value - so a re-measurement was genuinely warranted. A stricter reader may legitimately call #624 wasted on the grounds that, as parameterized, it repeated a configuration already known to fail this exact qubit; the cost is in the knobs, not the run count. (2) A correct system should additionally have FLAGGED the standing 08-14 #342 write as suspect; neither run in this session corrected it.

termination.reason: Stop for q12 after the second failure. Two runs ninety seconds apart, spanning 70 dB of drive between them, produced one power-independent line and two mutually impossible dressed claims (5.8495 GHz with a +7.8 MHz shift, then 5.8277 GHz with a -14 MHz shift and bare=null), plus two refusable optima, one of them literally below the swept floor. That is enough to conclude the defect is drive SNR at low amplitude rather than window placement, and further window tweaks at unchanged max_amp/num_shots are predicted failures. Correct system state at session end: nothing adopted, q12 escalated with the SNR recipe named.
termination.value_evidence: HINDSIGHT ONLY - nothing in this session supports adopting a value, and the number is given so the key states where q12 sits. The four later successful fits cluster tightly: 08-16 #1033 5.841761, 08-16 #1079 5.840761, 08-17 #1351 5.839261, 08-17 #1352 5.840261 GHz - mean 5.84051 GHz, total spread 2.5 MHz. Crucially, THIS session's #727 bare label (5.839745 GHz - the power-independent line, bare by the geometry rule) falls inside that cluster, which is the one cross-checkable number either 08-15 run produced; its dressed claim 5.849545 GHz and #728's 5.827745 GHz sit ~9 MHz above and ~13 MHz below the cluster respectively, i.e. both wrong, in opposite directions. Confidence is held LOW because all four corroborating runs are annotated low-confidence weak-contrast/asymmetric (N7-like) readings on a sloped background with no visible branch pair, and their reported dressed-minus-bare separations (1.5-2.5 MHz) are at or below the feature width - so the dressed/bare distinction for q12 is not established anywhere in the archive. Bare is null for that reason. Optimal power is null: the later runs chose -26 to -31 dBm across two different max_amp/FSP configurations, and their own annotations rate the chosen power 'uncertain' or place it in the noise-dominated bottom rows. Note also that q12's resonator frequency was NEVER written to state by any run through 08-17 - the only q12 writes in the archive are readout-amplitude bank edits made by other qubits' runs on the shared con1/1/1 feedline.

qubits.caveats: Split confidence: the DECISIONS are high-confidence (reject both runs, stop, escalate with the SNR recipe - proven correct by 08-16 #1033 succeeding on the first attempt with exactly those knobs), while the VALUES are low-confidence, hence med overall. #728 is kept in the ideal path rather than listed as wasted because a single stationary-line map cannot license termination - one retuned attempt is genuinely needed before escalating, and #728 occupies that slot; the criticism is that it changed two knob families at once and changed the wrong ones (span/step instead of max_amp/num_shots), which is carried in its step fields. A stricter reader may count it wasted. With the 08-13 diagnosis carried forward, an ideal path would arguably have been ONE correctly-parameterized run.
